lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Riverside Cinema | Box Office Attendant | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Sold tickets and concessions during evening shifts and balanced the cash drawer at close.
- Trained 3 new attendants on the ticketing system and the refund policy.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Check that the profile link is the exact, working URL you want employers to visit.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for US-based applications.
items.because: They disclose personal information that does not help assess your qualifications.

items.says: Consider removing the repeated location detail.
items.because: It may already be clear from your experience, and removing it can free space.

items.says: Keep the routine duties concise.
items.because: They should not crowd out analyst achievements.

items.says: Clarify your role in training the attendants if you did not own the whole process.
items.because: The line could imply you owned the whole process.

items.says: Separate what the dashboard enabled from what caused the repeat-purchase increase.
items.because: The line may imply the dashboard alone lifted the rate from 22% to 27%.

items.says: Confirm that the time-saving comparison measures the same reporting task.
A null customer name does not establish that a customer had no orders.
items.because: A missing order is normally identified through a null field from the orders side of a left join.

items.says: Make your individual contribution clearer and the opening easier to parse.
items.because: The current opening is hard to parse.

items.says: Explain the mechanism behind the 58%-to-81% change.
items.because: The metric could reflect changed attribution rules as well as improved data matching.

items.says: Be ready to identify which funded recommendations were yours.
Confirm how you measured the halving of ad hoc requests.
items.because: The result needs to be defensible.

items.says: Stopping the A/B test when daily checks first produced a p-value below 0.05 is invalid methodology.
items.because: It is an invalid use of a conventional fixed-sample significance test.

items.says: Clarify whether the staffing change followed your recommendation.
Clarify whether the hold-time comparison used comparable periods.
“Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in 2022.
Substantiate how the reduction in query errors was measured.
Focus the bullet on the automation and its 10-hour saving.
items.because: The long list of unrelated duties obscures the strongest result and makes your contribution harder to scan.

items.says: “12% mean absolute error” uses a percentage without specifying a valid percentage metric.
items.because: Mean absolute error alone is expressed in the units being forecast, not as a percentage.

items.says: The reduction from 300 to 200 is 33%, not 50%.
Make clear that the reduction came from a replay or simulation.
items.because: It was not an observed operational improvement.

items.says: The change from 60% to 75% is not a 15% increase.
items.because: It is 15 percentage points, or a 25% relative increase.

items.says: Define what counted as a forecast hit.
items.because: A reader may not know what “hit rate” means.

items.says: Ensure the comparison isolates the effect of the added features.
Distinguish your analysis from the pantry’s staffing decision.
Verify that the 50-to-20-minute comparison uses comparable Saturdays.
Clarify your role within the team of three.
items.because: Matching repeat visitors may have required judgments about incomplete handwritten records.

items.says: Give the one-page guide space only if space allows.
items.because: It is less important than the two results above.
